subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes, should OpenClaw preserve advertised `system.which`/`system.run` and make remote skill-bin probing readiness-aware, or should it skip/disable probes for co-located app nodes?
rationale: Current main has partial mitigations but no live proof that startup/reconnect probe timing is fixed, and the choice changes node exec compatibility, skill availability freshness, and operator-facing noise.

options.title: Defer and back off readiness-aware probes
options.body: Preserve the macOS app node command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

options.title: Skip only co-located app probes
options.body: Suppress the local gateway/app warning case while leaving remote macOS app timing and retry behavior to a separate follow-up.

options.title: Add an operator disable flag
options.body: Provide a global suppression knob, but accept new config surface and leave the underlying node-readiness behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Defer and back off readiness-aware probes
recommendation.body: Preserve the macOS app node command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's history is strongest around gateway node command policy and the product/security boundary for remote execution behavior.
